summary: Tested the operations_operator vs developer_ops role split (API matrix and UI), the 4-step Update wizard, the SERVICE_ISSUE guided flow, the maintenance bypass, audit and cleanup. Backend pytest: 65 of 66 passed (new test_cc_operator_role.py plus the iteration 90 and 91 suites). Every requested item passed in the UI. I found 2 real issues: (1) the operator can get out of SERVICE_ISSUE through begin-update, which gets around the developer_ops-only resolve; (2) POST /api/platform/auth/login returns 503 during Full Maintenance. I also found a dead 'Bring VIen back online' button for the operator during maintenance, plus small copy issues.

permission_matrix.developer_ops: 200 on all of the above (service-issue/resolve/maintenance/platform-config/data-ops verified)

critical.issue: Privilege escalation: while the state is SERVICE_ISSUE, operations_operator can call begin-update (e.g. kind RESOURCE). It returns 200 and the state goes SERVICE_ISSUE → UPDATING. The cron then auto-verifies and returns to NORMAL, so the operator gets around the developer_ops-only /resolve. Reproduced: tests/cc_probe_operator_escape.py. The UI makes this easy because the task-update card stays enabled during SERVICE_ISSUE. Fix: in begin_update, reject with 403 or 409 when the state is SERVICE_ISSUE and actor role != developer_ops. Also disable task-update for limited users in SERVICE_ISSUE. (During MAINTENANCE it is correctly rejected with 400.)

Returns 503 MAINTENANCE_MODE during Full Maintenance. '/api/platform/auth/login' is missing from system_state.ALLOW_PREFIXES. The middleware also has no role for an unauthenticated request. So a developer_ops or operator who is signed out cannot sign in through the platform endpoint until maintenance ends. The UI is unaffected only because /signin?internal=1 currently calls /api/auth/login, which is allowed. Fix: add '/api/platform/auth/login' to ALLOW_PREFIXES.

minor.issue: Bypass is only `role in OPS_ROLES`. operations_operator gets through on /api/developer/* only because of ALLOW_PREFIXES. Any non-developer API the operator UI might call during maintenance gets a 503. Consider OPERATOR_ROLES for consistency with the frontend's RoleRoute platformRole.
The generic login also accepts developer_ops/operations_operator accounts. Check that this is intended, since the platform login is meant to be the separate path.

ui_bugs.issue: The operator sees 'Recommended: Bring VIen back online' with a simple-recommended-run button. Clicking it calls setWiz('offline'), but OfflineWizard is not rendered for limited users, so nothing happens. Hide the button or route it to the contact-developer message. The same dead path exists for rec 'resolve' (SERVICE_ISSUE where the last check passed → setWiz('recover'), and RecoverWizard is not rendered for limited users).

The simple-contact-developer box is rendered at the bottom of the page (top ≈1400px), below the Recent activity section. After 'Take me there' the operator sees no visible feedback without scrolling. Scroll it into view, or render it near the attention section or as a dialog.

issues: The dialog description still says 'Three steps: prepare VIen, publish the update, let VIen verify itself.' but the wizard now has 4 steps.
The CheckWizard failure text tells the operator 'If this continues, use “Recover from a problem”', which the operator cannot do.
In HelpWizard, the 'stop' advice says 'Use “Take VIen temporarily offline”' and the 'login' advice says 'use “Recover from a problem”'. For operators the advice should point to Contact developer.

The history row title says 'problem resolved by the operator · Performed by Operations Operator' even when developer_ops performed the resolve, because the actor shown is the one who began the update. This is ambiguous for audit readers.

passed_ui_checks: Operator login /signin?internal=1 → /developer in SIMPLE; with localStorage vien_cc_mode=ADVANCED preset (also after a reload) there is no cc-mode-toggle, no dev-tabs and no cc-goto-advanced; cc-limited-badge and cc-limited-note are visible; only task-update/message/check/help are shown (no task-offline/task-recover)

Update wizard: progress shows Choose/Prepare VIen/Publish/Verification; step 2 contains 'does not install or publish anything' and 'The update is NOT published by this button.'; the button is 'Prepare VIen'; step 3 shows publish steps with 0 links; step 4 shows verification; the status hero shows 'VIen is being updated.'; the banner notice kind is UPDATE; history shows 'Software update in progress · Performed by Operations Operator · TEST_op update'
Help 'stop' → simple-contact-developer (no offline wizard); Help 'message' → wiz-message; the operator posted the message, patient /portal showed global-announcement, and the operator removed it

SERVICE_ISSUE as operator: one simple-recommended-run 'Run Check VIen' with no recover; after the failed check: simple-issue-persists 'The problem is still present.' with contact and recheck and no recover; contact text is shown; recheck reopens wiz-check
SERVICE_ISSUE as developer_ops: simple-issue-recover is shown after the failed check; after clearing expected_commit: simple-issue-passing + simple-issue-resolve → RecoverWizard → RESOLVE → NORMAL
developer_ops: cc-mode-toggle and all 6 task cards in SIMPLE; ADVANCED shows dev-tabs (OVERVIEW/FEATURES/PUBLIC SITE/OPERATIONS/DATA OPS) and OPERATIONS dep-ops with technical controls
Full Maintenance: the operator opens /developer (no maintenance screen); patient /portal shows maintenance-screen
Audit: announcement_published, announcement_removed and deployment_state_changed rows have actor_role operations_operator
action_items: HIGH: Block operations_operator from begin-update while the state is SERVICE_ISSUE (backend) and disable task-update for limited users in SERVICE_ISSUE (frontend)
HIGH: Add '/api/platform/auth/login' to system_state.ALLOW_PREFIXES so platform sign-in works during Full Maintenance
MEDIUM: Hide or redirect the simple-recommended-run 'Bring VIen back online' button (MAINTENANCE) and the 'Mark as resolved' recommendation for limited users; it is currently a dead button
LOW: Fix the Update wizard description ('Three steps' → four), make the operator copy in CheckWizard/HelpWizard role-aware, and scroll the contact-developer box into view
critical_code_review_comments: deployment.begin_update has no role or state guard that separates operator from developer_ops; SERVICE_ISSUE is the only state an operator must not leave
maintenance_mode_gate uses OPS_ROLES while the frontend treats both platform roles as exempt; align on OPERATOR_ROLES
SimpleOps renders recommendation buttons from attention() without checking `limited`; REC targets 'online' and 'resolve' map to wizards that are not mounted for limited users

success_rate.backend: 98% (65/66; the 1 failure is the real platform-login-during-maintenance bug)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of the requested flows passed; 1 dead-button bug and copy issues found

seed_data_creation: None. Only TEST_-prefixed notes and announcements, which were removed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest -n0 tests/test_cc_operator_role.py tests/test_cc_simple_mode_api.py tests/test_deployment_state*.py. test_maintenance_operator_access is expected to fail until /api/platform/auth/login is allow-listed. To check the escalation fix, run tests/cc_probe_operator_escape.py (it leaves MAINTENANCE ON at the end; EXIT afterwards via /api/auth/login with the devops token, since platform login gets a 503 during maintenance). cc_setup_issue.py issue|clear|resolve drives the SERVICE_ISSUE state. Final state: NORMAL, maintenance OFF, no announcement.
rca of the issue: Escalation: begin-update is guarded by OPERATOR_ROLES and dep_mod.begin_update allows the SERVICE_ISSUE → UPDATING transition (the earlier state is marked SUPERSEDED). The cron then verifies 3× OK and goes to NORMAL. Platform login 503: system_state.ALLOW_PREFIXES contains '/api/auth/login' but not '/api/platform/auth/login'; the unauthenticated request has role=None → 503.
